subproblem.title: C¹ approximation of Lipschitz functions on ℝ^m, value form (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5)
subproblem.statement:
Let m ∈ ℕ, K ≥ 0 and let u : ℝ^m → ℝ be K-Lipschitz (ℝ^m = Euclid m with Lebesgue measure L^m = volume). Then for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is a function G : ℝ^m → ℝ of class C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 G) with L^m({y ∈ ℝ^m : u(y) ≠ G(y)}) < ε.
(This is the part of Simon's C¹ Approximation Theorem, Ch. 2, 1.5, that concerns values; the companion statement about gradients is not needed.)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (u : Euclid m → ℝ) (K : NNReal), LipschitzWith K u → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ G : Euclid m → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 G ∧ volume {y | u y ≠ G y} < ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 2, proof of Theorem 1.5 (chapter-02.txt lines 246–262), with Rademacher's theorem 1.4 and Whitney's extension theorem 1.6 (lines 59–64, 170–185). Notation: L^m = volume on Euclid m, |·| the Euclidean norm, Du(x) = fderiv ℝ u x.

1. Reductions. If m = 0, Euclid 0 is a single point, so u is constant and G := u (ContDiff ℝ 1 of a constant map) gives {u ≠ G} = ∅. Assume m ≥ 1. If ε = ∞, run the argument below with ε replaced by 1; the resulting set has measure < 1 < ∞. So assume 0 < ε < ∞.
 [Imports: SimonGMT Chapter02.WhitneyExtension (Whitney; it builds from source, as there is no prebuilt .olean) and Chapter01.Lusin, or Mathlib's Lusin and Egorov (MeasureTheory.Function.Egorov).]

2. Rademacher (Ch. 2, 1.4; Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt, or SimonGMT Chapter02.rademacher_ae_differentiableAt). The set B := {x : u is differentiable at x} is Borel (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt) and L^m(ℝ^m ∖ B) = 0. The map x ↦ Du(x) is Borel (measurable_fderiv), and ‖Du(x)‖ ≤ K on B.

3. Lusin. Let S_j := {x : j ≤ |x| < j+1} (j ∈ ℕ), Borel shells of finite measure. For each j and each coordinate l = 1, …, m, apply Lusin's theorem for real-valued measurable maps on a finite-measure set (SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable, or Mathlib's Lusin) to x ↦ Du(x)e_l on S_j ∩ B. This gives a closed C_{j,l} ⊆ S_j ∩ B with L^m((S_j ∩ B) ∖ C_{j,l}) < ε·2^{-j-3}/m and Du(·)e_l continuous on C_{j,l}. Put C_j := ⋂_l C_{j,l} and C := ⋃_j C_j. The family (C_j) is locally finite, since a bounded set meets finitely many shells, so C is closed, C ⊆ B, and L^m(ℝ^m ∖ C) ≤ Σ_j L^m(S_j ∖ C_j) < ε/2. Du|_C is continuous: it is continuous on each closed C_j, and near any point of C only finitely many C_j occur.

4. Remainders. For x, y ∈ C with y ≠ x put R(x, y) := (u(y) − u(x) − Du(x)(y − x))/|y − x|. For k ≥ 1 let
   η_k(x) := sup{|R(x, y)| : y ∈ C, 0 < |y − x| < 1/k}   (sup ∅ := 0) for x ∈ C, and η_k(x) := 0 for x ∉ C.
   Then 0 ≤ η_k ≤ 2K, η_k(x) is non-increasing in k, and η_k(x) → 0 for every x ∈ C because u is differentiable at x ∈ C ⊆ B. Each η_k is Borel on ℝ^m. R is continuous on {(x, y) ∈ C × C : x ≠ y}, because u is continuous and Du|_C is continuous. So η_k|_C is a supremum of continuous functions over relatively open conditions, hence lower semicontinuous on C. Thus {η_k > t} = (O_t ∩ C) ∪ (ℝ^m ∖ C if t < 0) with O_t open, and C is closed.

5. Egorov. For each j apply Egorov's theorem (Mathlib tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto) to (η_k) on the finite-measure set C_j ⊆ S_j, with tolerance ε·2^{-j-5}. This gives a measurable A₀^j ⊆ C_j with L^m(C_j ∖ A₀^j) < ε·2^{-j-5} and η_k → 0 uniformly on A₀^j. By inner regularity of L^m on the finite-measure set A₀^j, choose a closed A^j ⊆ A₀^j with L^m(A₀^j ∖ A^j) < ε·2^{-j-5}. Put A := ⋃_j A^j. It is closed (a locally finite union of closed sets), A ⊆ C, and L^m(C ∖ A) < ε/4, so L^m(ℝ^m ∖ A) < ε/2 + ε/4 < ε. Moreover η_k → 0 uniformly on A ∩ B_R(0) for every R > 0, since this set lies in finitely many A^j.

6. Whitney's condition (Ch. 2, 1.6 (*); in SimonGMT this is the structure HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A u Du). (i) u is continuous on A. (ii) Du is continuous on A ⊆ C. (iii) Let K' ⊆ A be compact and ε' > 0. K' is bounded, so η_k → 0 uniformly on K'; choose k with η_k ≤ ε' on K' and put δ := 1/k. Then for x ∈ K', y ∈ A with |x − y| < δ: |u(y) − u(x) − Du(x)(y − x)| ≤ ε'|y − x| (trivial if y = x, and |R(x, y)| ≤ η_k(x) ≤ ε' otherwise).

7. Whitney extension (Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6; SimonGMT Chapter02.exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney, applied to the closed set A, h := u, D := Du): there is G : ℝ^m → ℝ with ContDiff ℝ 1 G and G = u on A. (If A = ∅ any constant G works.)

8. Conclusion. {y : u(y) ≠ G(y)} ⊆ ℝ^m ∖ A, so L^m({u ≠ G}) ≤ L^m(ℝ^m ∖ A) < ε. ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to 0 < ε < ∞.
Rademacher: u is differentiable off an L^m-null Borel set B^c; Du is Borel.
Lusin, coordinatewise on bounded shells: a closed C ⊆ B with L^m(ℝ^m ∖ C) < ε/2 and Du|_C continuous.
Define the Whitney remainders η_k on C; η_k ↓ 0 pointwise.
Egorov plus inner regularity: closed A ⊆ C, L^m(ℝ^m ∖ A) < ε, with η_k → 0 uniformly on bounded parts of A.
This is Whitney's C¹ compatibility condition for (u|_A, Du|_A).
Whitney extension gives a C¹ G with G = u on A, so L^m({u ≠ G}) < ε.

audit.reason: The proposition matches the global value-approximation statement, including zero dimension and infinite tolerance. The shellwise Lusin/Egorov construction produces a closed Whitney-compatible set with the required error bound; the checked Whitney theorem supplies the extension.

subproblem.title: At a Lebesgue density point, every unit direction is a limit of secant directions into the set
subproblem.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, Z ⊆ ℝ^d an arbitrary set and y ∈ ℝ^d a Lebesgue density point of Z in the sense that L^d(Z ∩ B̄_r(y))/L^d(B̄_r(y)) → 1 as r ↓ 0 (L^d = volume on Euclid d, outer measure; B̄_r(y) = closedBall y r). Then for every v ∈ ℝ^d with |v| = 1 there is a sequence (y_i) in Z ∖ {y} with y_i → y and (y_i − y)/|y_i − y| → v.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (Z : Set (Euclid d)) (y : Euclid d), Tendsto (fun r => volume (Z ∩ closedBall y r) / volume (closedBall y r)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1) → ∀ v : Euclid d, ‖v‖ = 1 → ∃ ys : ℕ → Euclid d, (∀ i, ys i ∈ Z ∧ ys i ≠ y) ∧ Tendsto ys atTop (𝓝 y) ∧ Tendsto (fun i => ‖ys i - y‖⁻¹ • (ys i - y)) atTop (𝓝 v)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the density-point argument behind parent Steps 3(a) and 3(c) (“there are y_k ∈ Y_j with y_k → y and (y_k − y)/|y_k − y| → e”).

1. Trivial case. If d = 0 there is no unit vector, so the claim is vacuous. Assume d ≥ 1, and fix v with |v| = 1.

2. A ball inside the cone. Let 0 < η ≤ 1 and r > 0, and put B := B_{ηr/4}(y + (r/2)v) (open ball). Write z − y = (r/2)v + w with |w| < ηr/4 for z ∈ B.
 (a) |z − y| ≤ r/2 + ηr/4 < r, so B ⊆ B̄_r(y).
 (b) |z − y| ≥ r/2 − ηr/4 ≥ r/4 > 0, so z ≠ y.
 (c) With s := r/2 and u := z − y = sv + w: ||u| − s| = ||sv + w| − |sv|| ≤ |w|. Hence
 |u/|u| − v| ≤ |u|·|1/|u| − 1/s| + |u/s − v| = ||u| − s|/s + |w|/s ≤ 2|w|/s < η.

3. Measure of the ball. By translation invariance and scaling of Lebesgue measure, L^d(B) = (η/4)^d L^d(B̄_r(y)), with 0 < L^d(B̄_r(y)) < ∞ (closed balls and open balls of the same radius have equal measure). [Lean: Measure.addHaar_ball / addHaar_closedBall; Nontrivial (Euclid d) follows from v ≠ 0. Only monotonicity of the outer measure and measure_diff for the measurable B are needed, so Z may be arbitrary.] Let κ := (η/4)^d ∈ (0, 1].

4. Hitting the ball. By the density hypothesis there is r₀ > 0 such that L^d(Z ∩ B̄_r(y)) > (1 − κ)L^d(B̄_r(y)) for all 0 < r < r₀. For such r, Z ∩ B ≠ ∅. Otherwise Z ∩ B̄_r(y) ⊆ B̄_r(y) ∖ B, and since B is measurable with B ⊆ B̄_r(y) (step 2(a)), L^d(Z ∩ B̄_r(y)) ≤ L^d(B̄_r(y)) − L^d(B) = (1 − κ)L^d(B̄_r(y)) (monotonicity of the outer measure), a contradiction.

5. The sequence. For i ≥ 1 apply step 4 with η := 1/i and some r = r_i < min(r₀(1/i), 1/i). Pick y_i ∈ Z ∩ B_{r_i/(4i)}(y + (r_i/2)v). By step 2: y_i ≠ y, |y_i − y| < r_i < 1/i, and |(y_i − y)/|y_i − y| − v| < 1/i. Hence y_i → y and (y_i − y)/|y_i − y| → v (index the sequence by i ∈ ℕ, e.g. using i + 1). ∎
proof_key_steps: d = 0 is vacuous; fix a unit v.
The ball B_{ηr/4}(y + (r/2)v) lies in B̄_r(y) ∖ {y}, inside the η-cone around v.
Its measure is the fixed fraction (η/4)^d of L^d(B̄_r(y)).
Density 1 forces Z to meet this ball for all small r.
Choose η = 1/i and r_i < min(r₀(η), 1/i) to get y_i → y with directions → v.

audit.reason: The cone-ball argument proves the exact sequence conclusion. Its measure comparison uses measurability only of the balls, so the absence of a measurability hypothesis on Z is legitimate.

subproblem.title: Approximate tangent space of a compact C¹ image at an interior regular point
subproblem.statement: Let k, P ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^k open, χ : ℝ^k → ℝ^P of class C¹ on V (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 χ V), C ⊆ V compact with χ injective on C, and y ∈ int C with Dχ(y) = fderiv ℝ χ y injective. Then χ(C) has approximate tangent space Q := Dχ(y)(ℝ^k) (= LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ χ y)) at χ(y) in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (χ '' C) (χ y) Q): dim Q = k and, for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{η_{χ(y),r}(χ(C))} f dH^k → ∫_Q f dH^k as r ↓ 0, where η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹(z − x) and H^k = μHE[k].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (k P : ℕ) (V C : Set (Euclid k)) (χ : Euclid k → Euclid P) (y : Euclid k), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 χ V → IsCompact C → C ⊆ V → InjOn χ C → y ∈ interior C → Injective (fderiv ℝ χ y) → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (χ '' C) (χ y) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ χ y : Euclid k →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P))

It is made explicit here with the area formula of Ch. 2, §3. Notation: x := χ(y), A := Dχ(y), Jχ(z) := (det(Dχ(z)ᵀDχ(z)))^{1/2} (SimonGMT areaJacobianAt χ z), JA := (det AᵀA)^{1/2}.

subproblem.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and T ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U (n+1)). Suppose T is represented by the integer multiplicity triple RT = (M, θ, ξ) in U of dimension n+1, and ∂T by the triple RB = (M', θ', ξ') in U of dimension n:
 T(η) = ∫_M θ⟨η, ξ⟩ dH^{n+1} for η ∈ 𝒟^{n+1}(U), and ∂T(ω) = T(dω) = ∫_{M'} θ'⟨ω, ξ'⟩ dHⁿ for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be L-Lipschitz, and g : ℝ^P → ℝ^P Borel with |g| ≤ L. Write T_xM := approxTangentPlane (n+1) M x and γ_{a,b}(s) := min{1, max{0, (b − s)/(b − a)}}. Assume the weak-limit property (G5):
 for all a < b, every sequence (h_k) of C¹ functions ℝ^P → ℝ with ‖Dh_k‖ ≤ c converging uniformly on ℝ^P to γ_{a,b}∘f, and every Borel W : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with |W| ≤ c', W = 0 outside some compact K ⊆ U, and W(x) ∈ T_xM for H^{n+1}-a.e. x ∈ M, we have ∫_M θ Dh_k[W] dH^{n+1} → ∫_{M∩{a<f<b}} θ·(−(b − a)⁻¹⟨g, W⟩) dH^{n+1}.
Then for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and all real a < b:
 ∫_{M'} θ'·γ_{a,b}(f)·⟨ω, ξ'⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_M θ·γ_{a,b}(f)·⟨dω, ξ⟩ dH^{n+1} − (b − a)⁻¹ ∫_{M∩{a<f<b}} θ·⟨g♭ ∧ ω, ξ⟩ dH^{n+1}.
Here dω = exteriorDerivative ω, ⟨α, ζ⟩ = ζ(α), Hᵏ = μHE[k], and g♭ ∧ ω := alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ g(x)).smulRight ω(x)); all integrals are Bochner integrals.

Source: parent Step 9 (a)–(c) and (e), and Step 0; Simon Ch. 6, proof of Lemma 4.5(2), displays (1)–(4) (chapter-06.txt lines 1235–1300). Fix ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and a < b. Put γ := γ_{a,b}, h := γ∘f and K := tsupport ω (compact, K ⊆ U).

0. Preliminaries.
 (a) Orientation a.e. By the field `orients` of RT and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces (Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1); HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), for H^{n+1}-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) is a unit orientation of T_xM: the space Q given by `orients` equals approxTangentPlane (n+1) M x. Likewise for RB.
 (b) Unit orientations have norm ≤ 1. If ζ is a unit orientation of a k-dimensional subspace (orthonormal τ), then |ζ(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ ∏|τ_i| = ‖α‖ (ContinuousMultilinearMap.le_opNorm).
 (c) Mass bounds. θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K'} θ dH^{n+1} < ∞ for compact K' ⊆ U (locallyIntegrable_mult). Same for RB.
 (d) Integrability. If β is a continuous k-form with tsupport β ⊆ K' (compact ⊆ U), then x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(β(x)) is H^{n+1}⌞M-integrable, bounded by sup‖β‖·θ1_{K'} a.e. It is a.e. strongly measurable because ξ is, β is continuous, and evaluation is continuous bilinear. Same for RB with k = n.
 (e) Strongly measurable version. ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H^{n+1}⌞M (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient). Let ξ₁ := RT.aestronglyMeasurable_orient.mk, a strongly measurable map with ξ₁ = ξ H^{n+1}-a.e. on M. Put ξ₀(x) := ξ₁(x) if ‖ξ₁(x)‖ ≤ 1 and ξ₀(x) := 0 otherwise. {‖ξ₁‖ ≤ 1} is measurable, so ξ₀ is strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.piecewise). By (a) and (b), ξ₀ = ξ H^{n+1}-a.e. on M, and ‖ξ₀(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x.

So work with StronglyMeasurable maps and their compositions with continuous (bi)linear maps (Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable, StronglyMeasurable.prodMk), not with “Borel ⇒ strongly measurable”. Real-, ℝ^P- or [0,∞]-valued strongly measurable maps are measurable (.measurable).]

1. Mollified cut-offs. h takes values in [0, 1] and is (L/(b − a))-Lipschitz. Let ρ be a smooth mollifier (C^∞, ≥ 0, ∫ρ = 1, spt ρ ⊆ B_1(0)), ρ_δ := δ^{−P}ρ(·/δ), δ_k := 1/(k+1), and h_k := h ∗ ρ_{δ_k}. Then:
 - h_k is C^∞, in particular C¹;
 - 0 ≤ h_k ≤ 1;
 - h_k is (L/(b − a))-Lipschitz (average of translates of h), so ‖Dh_k(x)‖ ≤ L/(b − a);
 - |h_k(x) − h(x)| ≤ ∫ρ_{δ_k}(z)|h(x − z) − h(x)|dz ≤ (L/(b − a))δ_k, so h_k → h uniformly on ℝ^P.

2. Leibniz identity for smooth cut-offs.
 - h_kω is C^∞ with tsupport(h_kω) ⊆ K ⊆ U and compact support, so h_kω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
 - By the product rule, fderiv(h_k•ω)(x) = Dh_k(x).smulRight ω(x) + h_k(x)•Dω(x). By linearity of alternatizeUncurryFin, d(h_kω) = dh_k∧ω + h_k dω, where dh_k∧ω := alternatizeUncurryFin(Dh_k(x).smulRight ω(x)) and exteriorDerivative = extDeriv = alternatizeUncurryFin ∘ fderiv.
 - RB represents ∂T, ∂T(η) = T(dη), and RT represents T. All three integrands are integrable by 0(d). Hence
 (i) ∫_{M'} θ' h_k ξ'(ω) dHⁿ = RB.action(h_kω) = T(d(h_kω)) = ∫_M θ ξ(dh_k∧ω) dH^{n+1} + ∫_M θ h_k ξ(dω) dH^{n+1}.

3. Outer terms. h_k → h pointwise, |θ'h_kξ'(ω)| ≤ θ'|ξ'(ω)| (integrable on M') and |θh_kξ(dω)| ≤ θ|ξ(dω)| (integrable on M). By dominated convergence,
 ∫_{M'} θ'h_kξ'(ω) → ∫_{M'} θ'hξ'(ω) and ∫_M θh_kξ(dω) → ∫_M θhξ(dω).

4. The middle term (Simon's display (3)). Let e_1, …, e_P be the standard basis and
 Ṽ(x) := Σ_{l=1}^{P} ξ₀(x)(e_l♭∧ω(x)) e_l.
 - Ṽ is measurable: each coefficient x ↦ ξ₀(x)(e_l♭∧ω(x)) is strongly measurable, as continuous bilinear evaluation applied to the strongly measurable ξ₀ and the continuous x ↦ e_l♭∧ω(x). Ṽ vanishes outside K, since ω = 0 there.
 - |Ṽ(x)| ≤ Σ_l ‖e_l♭∧ω(x)‖ ≤ P(n+1) sup‖ω‖ =: c', using ‖β∧α‖ ≤ (n+1)‖β‖‖α‖ from the alternating-sum formula.

 (c) By (a) with β = Dh_k(x), and ξ = ξ₀ a.e. on M: ξ(x)(dh_k(x)∧ω(x)) = Dh_k(x)[Ṽ(x)] for H^{n+1}-a.e. x ∈ M.
 (d) Apply (G5) with this a < b, the sequence h_k (step 1, c := L/(b − a)), W := Ṽ, K and c'. It gives
 ∫_M θ ξ(dh_k∧ω) dH^{n+1} = ∫_M θ Dh_k[Ṽ] dH^{n+1} → ∫_{M∩{a<f<b}} θ·(−(b − a)⁻¹⟨g, Ṽ⟩) dH^{n+1}.
 (e) By (a) with β = g(x)♭ = innerSL ℝ g(x): ⟨g(x), Ṽ(x)⟩ = ξ₀(x)(g(x)♭∧ω(x)) = ξ(x)(g(x)♭∧ω(x)) for a.e. x ∈ M. Pulling out the constant, the limit in (d) equals −(b − a)⁻¹∫_{M∩{a<f<b}} θ ξ(g♭∧ω) dH^{n+1}.

5. Passing to the limit (Simon's display after (4), with t = b and ε = b − a). Let k → ∞ in (i) and use steps 3 and 4. Uniqueness of limits gives
 ∫_{M'} θ' h ξ'(ω) dHⁿ = −(b − a)⁻¹∫_{M∩{a<f<b}} θ ξ(g♭∧ω) dH^{n+1} + ∫_M θ h ξ(dω) dH^{n+1}.
 Since h(x) = γ(f(x)) = min{1, max{0, (b − f(x))/(b − a)}}, this is the claimed identity, after rearranging the multiplications inside the integrands. ∎

Leibniz: d(h_kω) = dh_k∧ω + h_k dω, and ∂T(h_kω) = T(d(h_kω)) gives identity (i).

subproblem.title: Co-area formula on one C¹ chart piece for a function that is C¹ along the chart
subproblem.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Let V ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} be open and ψ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P be C¹ on V and injective on V, with Dψ(y) injective for every y ∈ V. Let C ⊆ V be compact and Y ⊆ C Borel. Let F : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ be C¹ and f : ℝ^P → ℝ satisfy f(ψ(y)) = F(y) for y ∈ Y. Let G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be Borel such that for every y ∈ Y: G(ψ(y)) ∈ Dψ(y)(ℝ^{n+1}) and ⟨G(ψ(y)), Dψ(y)e⟩ = DF(y)e for all e ∈ ℝ^{n+1}. (G is the tangential gradient of f on ψ(Y).) For t ∈ ℝ put S_t := ψ(Y) ∩ {x : G(x) ≠ 0} ∩ f⁻¹(t). Then for every Borel φ : ℝ^P → [0, ∞]:
 - the function t ↦ ∫_{S_t} φ dHⁿ is a.e.-measurable for Lebesgue measure on ℝ, and
 - ∫_ℝ ∫_{S_t} φ dHⁿ dt = ∫_{ψ(Y)} |G| φ dH^{n+1}.
Here Hᵏ = μHE[k] and all integrals are lower integrals in [0, ∞].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V C Y : Set (Euclid (n + 1))) (ψ : Euclid (n + 1) → Euclid P) (F : Euclid (n + 1) → ℝ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (G : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → InjOn ψ V → (∀ y ∈ V, Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ y)) → IsCompact C → C ⊆ V → MeasurableSet Y → Y ⊆ C → ContDiff ℝ 1 F → (∀ y ∈ Y, f (ψ y) = F y) → (∀ y ∈ Y, G (ψ y) ∈ LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ y : Euclid (n + 1) →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) ∧ ∀ e : Euclid (n + 1), inner ℝ (G (ψ y)) (fderiv ℝ ψ y e) = fderiv ℝ F y e) → Measurable G → ∀ φ : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable φ → AEMeasurable (fun t => ∫⁻ x in ψ '' Y ∩ {x | G x ≠ 0} ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, φ x ∂μHE[n]) ∧ ∫⁻ t, (∫⁻ x in ψ '' Y ∩ {x | G x ≠ 0} ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, φ x ∂μHE[n]) = ∫⁻ x in ψ '' Y, ‖G x‖ₑ * φ x ∂μHE[n + 1]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent Step 4(a) for one piece (Simon Ch. 3, 2.8–2.9; Ch. 2, 3.2, 3.5, 4.11–4.13, 6.3, 6.6). The parent combines:
 - the area formula for ψ;
 - the area formula for ψ restricted to the level sets Γ_t;
 - the Jacobian identity |g|J = |∇F|J_Γ;
 - the Euclidean co-area formula, obtained “from the implicit function theorem, Fubini and the area formula after locally straightening F to a coordinate function”.
These are carried out together below, in local coordinates in which F is one coordinate.
Notation: A(y) := Dψ(y), Γ(y) := A(y)ᵀA(y) (positive definite on V). For a map Φ that is differentiable with injective derivative, JΦ := (det DΦᵀDΦ)^{1/2} > 0 (SimonGMT areaJacobianAt). For i ∈ {1, …, n+1} let drop_i : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝⁿ delete the i-th coordinate, and ins_i(z, s) ∈ ℝ^{n+1} insert s as i-th coordinate into z ∈ ℝⁿ.

[Imports: SimonGMT Chapter02.WeightedArea (weighted area formula, areaJacobianAt).]

1. Reduction to the regular part.
 - For y ∈ Y the hypothesis gives G(ψ(y)) = A(y)w for some w, and Γ(y)w = A(y)ᵀG(ψ(y)) = ∇F(y), because ⟨G(ψ(y)), A(y)e⟩ = DF(y)e for all e. So G(ψ(y)) = A(y)Γ(y)⁻¹∇F(y), and since A(y) is injective, G(ψ(y)) ≠ 0 ⇔ ∇F(y) ≠ 0.
 - Let O := {y ∈ V : ∇F(y) ≠ 0} (open, as F is C¹) and Y' := Y ∩ O. Using f∘ψ = F on Y: S_t = ψ(Y' ∩ F⁻¹(t)) for every t. Also |G|φ = 0 on ψ(Y ∖ Y'), and ψ(Y) = ψ(Y') ⊔ ψ(Y ∖ Y').
 - Images under ψ of Borel subsets of Y are Borel: Lusin–Souslin, since ψ is continuous and injective on the Borel set Y (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
 - Hence it suffices to prove: t ↦ ∫_{ψ(Y'∩F⁻¹(t))} φ dHⁿ is a.e.-measurable, and ∫_ℝ ∫_{ψ(Y'∩F⁻¹(t))} φ dHⁿ dt = ∫_{ψ(Y')} |G|φ dH^{n+1}.
 (G is only used through its values on ψ(Y), given by the formula above; the hypothesis Measurable G is not needed.)

2. Local straightening.
 - Let y₀ ∈ O and choose an index i with ∂_iF(y₀) ≠ 0. Define Θ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1} by Θ(y)_l := y_l for l ≠ i and Θ(y)_i := F(y). Θ is C¹ and DΘ(y₀) is invertible.
 - By the inverse function theorem (Mathlib HasStrictFDerivAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph) there are an open N with y₀ ∈ N ⊆ O and an open box B with Θ : N → B a C¹ diffeomorphism. B is a product: an open box D ⊆ ℝⁿ in the coordinates l ≠ i, and an open interval I in coordinate i. Let Ψ := (Θ|_N)⁻¹ : B → N. Then F(Ψ(w)) = w_i, and DΨ is invertible on B.
 - O is Lindelöf, so countably many such N, say N_q (q ∈ ℕ), cover O. Pad with empty sets if needed. Put Y_q := (Y' ∩ N_q) ∖ ⋃_{p<q} N_p. These are disjoint Borel sets with ⋃_q Y_q = Y'.

3. Reduction to one patch. Suppose that for every q:
 (*) t ↦ ∫_{ψ(Y_q∩F⁻¹(t))} φ dHⁿ is a.e.-measurable, and ∫_ℝ ∫_{ψ(Y_q∩F⁻¹(t))} φ dHⁿ dt = ∫_{ψ(Y_q)} |G|φ dH^{n+1}.
 - For every t, ψ(Y'∩F⁻¹(t)) is the disjoint union of the Borel sets ψ(Y_q∩F⁻¹(t)), so ∫_{ψ(Y'∩F⁻¹(t))} φ = Σ_q ∫_{ψ(Y_q∩F⁻¹(t))} φ (lintegral_iUnion).
 - A countable sum of a.e.-measurable [0,∞]-valued functions is a.e.-measurable, and ∫_ℝ Σ_q = Σ_q ∫_ℝ (lintegral_tsum).
 - Likewise ∫_{ψ(Y')} |G|φ = Σ_q ∫_{ψ(Y_q)} |G|φ.
 Summing (*) over q gives the claim of step 1.

4. One patch. Fix q, and let N, B = D × I (in the coordinates of step 2), Θ, Ψ be the data for N_q.
 - Φ := ψ∘Ψ : B → ℝ^P is C¹ and injective, and DΦ = A(Ψ)DΨ is injective.
 - Ŷ := Θ(Y_q) ⊆ B is Borel (Θ restricts to a homeomorphism N → B), and Ψ(Ŷ) = Y_q.
 - For s ∈ ℝ let Ŷ_s := {z ∈ D : ins_i(z, s) ∈ Ŷ} ⊆ ℝⁿ and Φ_s(z) := Φ(ins_i(z, s)) for z ∈ D. Φ_s is C¹ and injective, and DΦ_s(z) = DΦ(ins_i(z, s))∘ins_i(·, 0) is injective.
 - Since F(Ψ(w)) = w_i: ψ(Y_q) = Φ(Ŷ) and ψ(Y_q ∩ F⁻¹(s)) = Φ_s(Ŷ_s). For s ∉ I this set is empty.

5. Area formulas. Ch. 2, 3.2/3.5 is the weighted area formula for injective differentiable maps with injective derivative (SimonGMT Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_of_injective_derivative); on the parameter spaces μHE[n+1] = L^{n+1} and μHE[n] = Lⁿ. It gives
 ∫_{Φ(Ŷ)} |G|φ dH^{n+1} = ∫_Ŷ JΦ(w)·(|G|φ)(Φ(w)) dw,
 ∫_{Φ_s(Ŷ_s)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{Ŷ_s} JΦ_s(z)·φ(Φ_s(z)) dz   for every s ∈ I.

6. Jacobian identity: |G(Φ(w))|·JΦ(w) = JΦ_s(z) for w = ins_i(z, s) ∈ Ŷ.
 Let y := Ψ(w) ∈ Y_q, x := ψ(y), u := G(x). Then u ≠ 0, since y ∈ O.
 - The vectors a_l := DΦ(w)e_l (l ≠ i) and a_i := DΦ(w)e_i span A(y)(ℝ^{n+1}), because DΨ(w) is invertible. The a_l with l ≠ i are the columns of DΦ_s(z).
 - By the hypothesis on G and F(Ψ(w)) = w_i: ⟨u, a_l⟩ = DF(y)DΨ(w)e_l = ∂_l(F∘Ψ)(w), which is 0 for l ≠ i and 1 for l = i.
 - So u lies in the (n+1)-dimensional space A(y)(ℝ^{n+1}) and is orthogonal to the n-dimensional subspace E := span{a_l : l ≠ i}. Hence u/|u| spans E^⊥ ∩ A(y)(ℝ^{n+1}).
 - Gram determinant formula: the Gram determinant of n+1 vectors is the Gram determinant of n of them times the squared distance of the remaining one to their span, so (JΦ)² = (JΦ_s)²·dist(a_i, E)². [Equivalently: the matrix of DΦ(w) in orthonormal bases adapted to E ⊕ ℝ(u/|u|) is block upper triangular with corner entry ⟨a_i, u/|u|⟩.]
 - dist(a_i, E) = |⟨a_i, u/|u|⟩| = 1/|u|. Hence JΦ = JΦ_s/|u|.

7. Tonelli.
 - Let H(w) := 1_Ŷ(w)·φ(Φ(w))·JΦ_{w_i}(drop_i w) for w ∈ B, and H := 0 elsewhere. H ≥ 0 is Borel: φ is Borel, Φ is continuous, and w ↦ JΦ_{w_i}(drop_i w) is continuous on B.
 - By steps 5 and 6, ∫_{ψ(Y_q)} |G|φ dH^{n+1} = ∫_Ŷ JΦ·(|G|φ)∘Φ dw = ∫ H dL^{n+1}.
 - The map w ↦ (w_i, toLp(drop_i w)) is a volume-preserving measurable equivalence Euclid (n+1) ≃ ℝ × Euclid n. Compose PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp (= EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp), MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove (which splits off coordinate i first) and PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp on the second factor (MeasurePreserving.prod). The second factor is Euclid n, so μHE[n] = volume there for the slice area formula. By Tonelli (Measurable.lintegral_prod_right'), s ↦ ∫ H(ins_i(z, s)) dz is Borel and ∫ H dL^{n+1} = ∫_ℝ ∫_{Euclid n} H(ins_i(z, s)) dz ds.
 - For s ∈ I, step 5 gives ∫ H(ins_i(z, s)) dz = ∫_{Ŷ_s} JΦ_s·φ∘Φ_s dz = ∫_{ψ(Y_q∩F⁻¹(s))} φ dHⁿ. For s ∉ I both sides are 0.
 This proves (*) for patch q, with the inner integral even Borel in s. ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to Y' = Y ∩ {∇F ≠ 0}, where G(ψ y) = Dψ Γ⁻¹∇F ≠ 0. S_t = ψ(Y' ∩ F⁻¹(t)).
Straighten F near each regular point: Θ replaces coordinate i by F, Ψ = Θ⁻¹ on a box. Countable disjoint Borel patches Y_q.
Countable additivity and lintegral_tsum reduce to one patch.
On a patch, Φ = ψ∘Ψ parametrizes ψ(Y_q) and Φ(·, s) parametrizes the slice ψ(Y_q ∩ F⁻¹(s)).
Area formula for Φ and for each Φ(·, s).
Jacobian identity |G∘Φ|·JΦ = JΦ_s, since ⟨G, ∂_zΦ⟩ = 0, ⟨G, ∂_sΦ⟩ = 1 and the Gram determinant is base × height.
Tonelli via the volume-preserving split ℝ^{n+1} ≃ ℝⁿ × ℝ gives measurability in s and the co-area identity.

subproblem.title: Interior product of a unit orientation with a unit tangent vector (Simon Ch. 6, 4.3)
subproblem.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ and Q ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace. Let ζ be an (n+1)-vector, i.e. a continuous linear functional on (n+1)-covectors of ℝ^P (MultiVector P (n+1)), which is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q). This means: there is an orthonormal τ = (τ₀, …, τₙ) spanning Q with ζ(β) = β(τ) for all β, or ζ(β) = −β(τ) for all β. Let ν ∈ Q with |ν| = 1. Let ζ' be an n-vector (MultiVector P n) with ζ'(α) = ζ(ν♭ ∧ α) for every n-covector α. Here
 ν♭ ∧ α := ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ ν).smulRight α),
 that is, (ν♭∧α)(v₀, …, vₙ) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i ⟨ν, v_i⟩ α(v₀, …, v̂_i, …, vₙ).
Then ζ' is a unit orientation of Q ∩ ν^⊥ (IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' (Q ⊓ (ℝ∙ν)ᗮ)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ζ : MultiVector P (n + 1)) (ζ' : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ν : Euclid P), IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q → ν ∈ Q → ‖ν‖ = 1 → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ζ' α = ζ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ ν).smulRight α))) → IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' (Q ⊓ (ℝ ∙ ν)ᗮ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent Step 5 and Step 0(a); Simon Ch. 6, 4.3 (⟨v⌞w, a⟩ = ⟨v, w∧a⟩, and ξ⌞ν is a simple unit n-vector orienting T_xM_t).

1. Dimensions. τ is an orthonormal family of n+1 vectors spanning Q, so dim Q = n+1. Since ν ∈ Q and ν ≠ 0, Q = (ℝ∙ν) ⊕ (Q ⊓ (ℝ∙ν)ᗮ) orthogonally (Submodule.sup_orthogonal_inf_of_hasOrthogonalProjection applied to ℝ∙ν ≤ Q, with Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq or the orthogonal direct sum). Hence Q' := Q ∩ ν^⊥ = Q ⊓ (ℝ∙ν)ᗮ has dimension n. Let σ = (σ₁, …, σₙ) be an orthonormal basis of Q' (e.g. stdOrthonormalBasis of Q', reindexed by Fin n; for n = 0 the empty family). Then ρ := (ν, σ₁, …, σₙ) is an orthonormal family of n+1 vectors in Q, hence an orthonormal basis of Q, and span(range σ) = Q'.

2. Sign lemma (parent Step 0(a)). Write ρ_i = Σ_l m_{il} τ_l. The matrix (m_{il}) is orthogonal, since both families are orthonormal bases of Q, so det(m) = ε₀ ∈ {1, −1} (OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real). Every (n+1)-covector β, restricted to Q (the alternating map β.compLinearMap Q.subtype on Q), is a multiple of the determinant in the basis τ (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). So β(ρ₀, …, ρₙ) = det(m)·β(τ₀, …, τₙ) = ε₀ β(τ). With the sign ε₁ ∈ {1, −1} from IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q, we get ζ(β) = ε₁β(τ) = ε₁ε₀ β(ν, σ₁, …, σₙ) for every β. The sign ε := ε₁ε₀ does not depend on β.

3. Wedge expansion. Let α be an n-covector and put v₀ := ν, v_i := σ_i (i = 1, …, n), i.e. v = Fin.cons ν σ. By the formula for alternatizeUncurryFin (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_apply: alternatizeUncurryFin F v = Σ_i (−1)^i • F (v i) (Fin.removeNth i v)), by (innerSL ℝ ν)(w) = ⟨ν, w⟩ and by Fin.removeNth 0 (Fin.cons ν σ) = σ:
 (ν♭∧α)(v₀, …, vₙ) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i ⟨ν, v_i⟩ α(v without v_i) = ⟨ν, ν⟩ α(σ₁, …, σₙ) + Σ_{i=1}^{n} (−1)^i ⟨ν, σ_i⟩(…) = α(σ₁, …, σₙ),
 since ⟨ν, ν⟩ = 1 and ⟨ν, σ_i⟩ = 0 (σ_i ∈ ν^⊥).

4. Conclusion. For every n-covector α, ζ'(α) = ζ(ν♭∧α) = ε(ν♭∧α)(ν, σ₁, …, σₙ) = ε α(σ). σ is orthonormal with span(range σ) = Q ⊓ (ℝ∙ν)ᗮ, and either ζ' α = α σ for all α (ε = 1) or ζ' α = −α σ for all α (ε = −1). This is IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' (Q ⊓ (ℝ∙ν)ᗮ). ∎

subproblem.title: Countably rectifiable sets are covered by C¹ submanifolds up to a null set (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2, “only if”)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and let M ⊆ ℝ^P be countably m-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable m M: M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^m) with H^m(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz F_j : ℝ^m → ℝ^P; H^m = μHE[m]). Then there are a set N₀ ⊆ ℝ^P with H^m(N₀) = 0 and sets N_l ⊆ ℝ^P (l ∈ ℕ), each an embedded m-dimensional C¹ submanifold of ℝ^P in the sense of the contract (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m N_l: every point of N_l has an open W ∋ y and a C¹ map ψ on an open V ⊆ ℝ^m, injective on V, with ψ(V) = W ∩ N_l, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) compact for compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) injective for z ∈ V), such that M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_l N_l.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, proof of Lemma 1.2, “only if” part (chapter-03.txt lines 22–60), using the C¹ Approximation Theorem (sibling c1_approx, Lean dor_lmbsf_lipschitz_c1_approx) and the area formula of Ch. 2, §3. Notation: H^m = μHE[m]. On ℝ^m = Euclid m, H^m = L^m = volume (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). For a C¹ map G : ℝ^m → ℝ^P let Crit(G) := {y : DG(y) is not injective}.

[Imports: SimonGMT Chapter02.AreaCritical (critical images) and Chapter02.Lipschitz (Lipschitz images).]

1. By definition, M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_{j∈ℕ} F_j(ℝ^m), H^m(M₀) = 0, F_j : ℝ^m → ℝ^P K_j-Lipschitz.

2. Vector C¹ approximation. Fix j and i ≥ 1. If P = 0 put G_{ij} := F_j (a constant map, C¹). If P ≥ 1, each coordinate F_j^p := ⟨F_j, e_p⟩ (p = 1, …, P) is K_j-Lipschitz, so the sibling c1_approx (with ε = 1/(iP)) gives C¹ functions G_{ij}^p with L^m({F_j^p ≠ G_{ij}^p}) < 1/(iP). Let G_{ij} : ℝ^m → ℝ^P have coordinates G_{ij}^p; it is C¹ and {F_j ≠ G_{ij}} ⊆ ⋃_p {F_j^p ≠ G_{ij}^p} has L^m-measure < 1/i.

3. Z_j := ⋂_{i≥1} {F_j ≠ G_{ij}} has L^m(Z_j) ≤ 1/i for all i, so L^m(Z_j) = 0, and E_j := F_j(Z_j) satisfies H^m(E_j) ≤ K_j^m L^m(Z_j) = 0 (Lipschitz images: SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn). Every y ∉ Z_j has F_j(y) = G_{ij}(y) for some i, so F_j(ℝ^m) ⊆ E_j ∪ ⋃_i G_{ij}(ℝ^m). Hence
   M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j E_j ∪ ⋃_{i,j} G_{ij}(ℝ^m).   (1)

4. Critical images are null. For C¹ G, H^m(G(Crit(G))) = 0. This is the area formula of Ch. 2, 3.2 (H^m(G(A)) ≤ ∫_A JG dL^m, with JG = 0 exactly on Crit(G)). In SimonGMT it is Chapter02.area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero: μHE[finrank ℝ E] (G '' {x | DifferentiableAt ℝ G x ∧ ¬ Injective (fderiv ℝ G x)}) = 0. Here E = Euclid m, so finrank ℝ E = m (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), and every point is a differentiability point because G is C¹.

5. Regular points give embedded submanifolds. Let G be C¹ and x ∉ Crit(G). Put c := min_{|v|=1} |DG(x)v| > 0 if m ≥ 1, and c := 1 if m = 0. (For m = 0, ℝ^0 is a point, the annulus below is empty and W = ℝ^P.) Choose ρ > 0 with ‖DG(z) − DG(x)‖ ≤ c/2 for |z − x| ≤ 2ρ. By the mean value inequality on the convex ball B̄_{2ρ}(x), |G(a) − G(b) − DG(x)(a − b)| ≤ (c/2)|a − b| for a, b ∈ B̄_{2ρ}(x), hence |G(a) − G(b)| ≥ (c/2)|a − b|. So G is injective on B̄_{2ρ}(x), and DG(z) is injective for |z − x| ≤ 2ρ. Let N := G(B_ρ(x)). For every point of N use V := B_ρ(x), W := ℝ^P ∖ G(B̄_{2ρ}(x) ∖ B_ρ(x)) and ψ := G:
   - W is open, since B̄_{2ρ}(x) ∖ B_ρ(x) is compact and G is continuous;
   - N ⊆ W by injectivity of G on B̄_{2ρ}(x), so ψ(V) = N = W ∩ N, and every point of N lies in W;
   - ψ is C¹ on V, injective on V, and Dψ(z) is injective for z ∈ V;
   - properness: for compact K ⊆ W, V ∩ G⁻¹(K) = B̄_ρ(x) ∩ G⁻¹(K), because points of the sphere ∂B_ρ(x) ⊆ B̄_{2ρ}(x) ∖ B_ρ(x) are mapped outside W ⊇ K; this is a closed subset of the compact ball B̄_ρ(x), hence compact.
   Thus IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m N (this is Simon's “G_{ij}(B_δ(x)) is an n-dimensional C¹ submanifold”).

6. Lindelöf. The set ℝ^m ∖ Crit(G) is covered by the open balls B_ρ(x) of step 5. ℝ^m is second countable, so every subset is Lindelöf, and countably many of these balls, B_{ρ_s}(x_s) (s ∈ ℕ), cover it. Hence G(ℝ^m) ⊆ G(Crit(G)) ∪ ⋃_s G(B_{ρ_s}(x_s)).

7. Conclusion. Apply steps 4–6 to every G_{ij}. Put N₀ := M₀ ∪ ⋃_j E_j ∪ ⋃_{i,j} G_{ij}(Crit(G_{ij})); it is a countable union of H^m-null sets, so H^m(N₀) = 0. Enumerate the countably many sets G_{ij}(B_{ρ_s}(x_s)) as N_l, l ∈ ℕ (padding with N_l := ∅, which satisfies IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m vacuously). By (1) and step 6, M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_l N_l. ∎
proof_key_steps: Write M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃ F_j(ℝ^m) with Lipschitz F_j.
Coordinatewise c1_approx gives C¹ maps G_{ij} with L^m({F_j ≠ G_{ij}}) < 1/i.
Z_j = ⋂_i {F_j ≠ G_{ij}} is null and F_j(Z_j) is H^m-null, so M ⊆ null ∪ ⋃ G_{ij}(ℝ^m).
Images of the critical sets Crit(G_{ij}) are H^m-null (area formula; SimonGMT area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero).
Near a regular point, G(B_ρ(x)) is an embedded C¹ m-submanifold (injective on B̄_{2ρ}, W = ℝ^P ∖ G(annulus), properness).
Lindelöf: countably many such balls cover ℝ^m ∖ Crit(G). Collect the null sets into N₀ and enumerate the submanifolds.

Source: parent Step 4(b), first bullet, and Step 4(c), for one piece; Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 4.1(1),(2) and its proof; Ch. 2, 6.4 and Remark 4.4 (local graphs); Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 “if”. Notation: A(y) := Dψ(y), O := {y ∈ V : ∇F(y) ≠ 0} (open), Γ_t := O ∩ F⁻¹(t).

1. Description of S_t. Let y ∈ Y. The hypothesis gives G(ψ(y)) = A(y)w for some w ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and ⟨G(ψ(y)), A(y)e⟩ = DF(y)e for all e.
 - If G(ψ(y)) = 0 then DF(y) = 0.
 - If DF(y) = 0 then ⟨G(ψ(y)), A(y)w⟩ = 0, i.e. |G(ψ(y))|² = 0.
 So G(ψ(y)) ≠ 0 ⇔ y ∈ O. With f∘ψ = F on Y, S_t = ψ(Y ∩ Γ_t), and S_t is Borel (Lusin–Souslin, MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn: ψ is continuous and injective on the Borel set Y ∩ Γ_t).
 For y ∈ Y ∩ Γ_t and x = ψ(y) put T_x := A(y)(ker DF(y)). For v = A(y)e we have ⟨G(x), v⟩ = DF(y)e, so T_x = A(y)(ℝ^{n+1}) ∩ G(x)^⊥ = range Dψ(y) ⊓ (ℝ∙G(x))ᗮ. T_x is n-dimensional, since DF(y) ≠ 0 and A(y) is injective.

2. Local graph parametrizations of Γ_t (implicit function theorem). Let y₀ ∈ Γ_t and pick i with ∂_iF(y₀) ≠ 0. Straighten F as follows: Θ(y)_l := y_l (l ≠ i) and Θ(y)_i := F(y). By the inverse function theorem Θ is a C¹ diffeomorphism from an open N ∋ y₀, N ⊆ O, onto an open box D × I (D an open box in the coordinates l ≠ i, I an open interval), with inverse Ψ. Equivalently, by the implicit function theorem, Γ_t ∩ N is a C¹ graph over the coordinates l ≠ i. Put Λ(z) := Ψ(ins_i(z, t)) for z ∈ D, where ins_i inserts t as i-th coordinate; then Γ_t ∩ N = Λ(D). Λ is C¹ on D and injective, DΛ(z) is injective, and DΛ(z)(ℝⁿ) = ker DF(Λ(z)) (F∘Λ ≡ t and both spaces are n-dimensional). Choose a closed ball D̄' = B̄_ρ(z₀) ⊆ D, z₀ := Λ⁻¹(y₀). Γ_t is second countable, so there are countably many such data (D_k, Λ_k, B̄_{ρ_k}(z_k)), k ∈ ℕ, with Γ_t = ⋃_k Λ_k(B_{ρ_k}(z_k)). If Γ_t = ∅ then S_t = ∅ and (i), (ii) are trivial.

 - A_k is Borel (Lusin–Souslin) and A_k ⊆ Σ_k.
 - χ_k is C¹ on D_k and injective on D̄_k (ψ is injective on V ⊇ N and Λ_k is injective).
 - Dχ_k(z) = A(Λ_k z)DΛ_k(z) is injective with range A(y)(ker DF(y)) = T_x, where y = Λ_k(z) and x = χ_k(z).
 - By the sibling image_tangent (Lean dor_lmbsf_c1_image_approxTangent, with k := n, V := D_k, C := D̄_k, χ := χ_k), Σ_k has approximate tangent space T_{χ_k(z)} at χ_k(z) for every z ∈ B_{ρ_k}(z_k) = int D̄_k.
 - Apply (TL) with (U, A, B) := (ℝ^P, A_k, Σ_k): U = ℝ^P is open (isOpen_univ), both sets are Borel, A_k ⊆ Σ_k ⊆ ℝ^P, and Hⁿ(Σ_k ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(Σ_k) < ∞ (measure_mono). subproblem.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Let V ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} be open and ψ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P be C¹ on V and injective on V, with Dψ(y) injective for y ∈ V. Let C ⊆ V be compact, Y ⊆ C Borel, and F : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ C¹. Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be L-Lipschitz with f(ψ(y)) = F(y) for y ∈ Y. Let G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be Borel with, for every y ∈ Y, G(ψ(y)) ∈ Dψ(y)(ℝ^{n+1}) and ⟨G(ψ(y)), Dψ(y)e⟩ = DF(y)e for all e.
Let a < b and γ(s) := min{1, max{0, (b − s)/(b − a)}}. Let (h_k)_{k∈ℕ} be C¹ functions ℝ^P → ℝ with ‖Dh_k(x)‖ ≤ c for all k, x, converging uniformly on ℝ^P to γ∘f. Let w : ℝ^P → ℝ be integrable on ψ(Y) with respect to H^{n+1} = μHE[n+1]. Let W : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be Borel with |W| ≤ c', such that for H^{n+1}-a.e. x ∈ ψ(Y), W(x) ∈ Dψ(y)(ℝ^{n+1}) for the y ∈ Y with ψ(y) = x. Then
 lim_{k→∞} ∫_{ψ(Y)} w(x)·Dh_k(x)[W(x)] dH^{n+1}(x) = ∫_{ψ(Y)∩{a<f<b}} w(x)·(−(b − a)⁻¹⟨G(x), W(x)⟩) dH^{n+1}(x)
(Bochner integrals).

The constant c bounds ‖Dh_k‖, and κ ∈ {a, b} denotes a kink of γ.

[Imports: SimonGMT Chapter02.WeightedArea; Mathlib Analysis.Normed.Lp.SmoothApprox (Lp.dense_hasCompactSupport_contDiff) and MeasureTheory.Covering.Besicovitch (density theorem).]

1. Setup.
 - Choose δ > 0 with C' := cthickening δ C ⊆ V (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). C' is compact and C ⊆ int C'.
 - A and Γ⁻¹ are continuous on V, hence bounded on C' by some Λ'.
 - ψ is C¹ on a neighbourhood of the compact C', hence Lipschitz on C' with some constant Λ: a locally Lipschitz map is Lipschitz on compact sets (Lebesgue number argument).
 - u := h∘ψ and u_k := h_k∘ψ are Lipschitz on C' with constants LΛ/(b − a) and cΛ, and u_k → u uniformly on C'.
 - Let ū, ū_k be McShane extensions of u|_{C'}, u_k|_{C'} to ℝ^{n+1} with the same Lipschitz constants. On int C', ū_k = u_k is C¹ with |∇u_k| ≤ cΛ' (chain rule), and ū is differentiable L^{n+1}-a.e. (Rademacher).

2. Transfer to the chart.
 - Area measure. By SimonGMT Chapter02.map_withDensity_areaJacobian_eq (Ch. 2, 3.2): the push-forward under ψ of J·L^{n+1}⌞Y is H^{n+1}⌞ψ(Y). ψ is differentiable with injective derivative on Y ⊆ V and injective on Y. J > 0 on Y (areaJacobianAt_eq_zero_iff_not_injective), so L^{n+1}⌞Y and J·L^{n+1}⌞Y have the same null sets. Hence the tangency hypothesis pulls back: W(ψ(y)) ∈ A(y)(ℝ^{n+1}) for L^{n+1}-a.e. y ∈ Y (ae_of_ae_map).
 - The chart field. Put E(y) := Γ(y)⁻¹A(y)ᵀW(ψ(y)) for y ∈ C. It is Borel and bounded by Λ'²c'. At the y above, A(y)E(y) = W(ψ(y)).
 - Chain rule. ψ is differentiable at y ∈ V, so Dh_k(ψ(y))[W(ψ(y))] = Dh_k(ψ(y))[A(y)E(y)] = Du_k(y)[E(y)] for a.e. y ∈ Y.
 - Area formula for Bochner integrals with arbitrary integrand (SimonGMT Chapter02.integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative):
 ∫_{ψ(Y)} w Dh_k[W] dH^{n+1} = ∫_Y J(y)·w(ψ(y))·Dh_k(ψ(y))[W(ψ(y))] dy = ∫_{ℝ^{n+1}} ⟨Ŵ(y), ∇ū_k(y)⟩ dy,
 where Ŵ(y) := 1_Y(y)·J(y)·w(ψ(y))·E(y), and ∇ū_k = ∇u_k on Y ⊆ int C'.
 - Ŵ ∈ L¹(ℝ^{n+1}; ℝ^{n+1}): y ↦ J(y)w(ψ(y)) is integrable on Y (SimonGMT Chapter02.integrableOn_image_iff_integrableOn_areaJacobian_smul, as w is integrable on ψ(Y)), and E is bounded. Ŵ vanishes outside C ⊆ int C'.

3. Weak-* convergence of the chart gradients.
 - Integration by parts. Let Φ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1} be C¹ with compact support in int C'. Integrate by parts coordinatewise for Lipschitz functions against a compactly supported Lipschitz function (Mathlib LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq, with v = e_l), and use the uniform convergence ū_k → ū on spt Φ ⊆ C':
 ∫ ⟨Φ, ∇ū_k⟩ = −∫ (div Φ) ū_k → −∫ (div Φ) ū = ∫ ⟨Φ, ∇ū⟩.
 - Density. C¹ compactly supported fields are dense in L¹(ℝ^{n+1}; ℝ^{n+1}) (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Lp.dense_hasCompactSupport_contDiff). Let χ be a smooth cut-off with χ = 1 on C, spt χ ⊆ int C' and 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1. Since Ŵ = χŴ, for any such Φ, χΦ is admissible and ‖χΦ − Ŵ‖_{L¹} ≤ ‖Φ − Ŵ‖_{L¹}.
 - Uniform bounds. On int C', |∇ū_k| ≤ cΛ' and |∇ū| ≤ Lip(ū).
 - Conclusion. For ε > 0 pick an admissible Φ with ‖Ŵ − Φ‖_{L¹} < ε. Then limsup_k |∫⟨Ŵ, ∇ū_k − ∇ū⟩| ≤ ε(cΛ' + Lip(ū)). Hence ∫ ⟨Ŵ, ∇ū_k⟩ → ∫ ⟨Ŵ, ∇ū⟩.

4. Identification of ∇ū on Y (parent Steps 3(c), 3(d)).
 (a) Agreement lemma. Let v₁, v₂ be Lipschitz on ℝ^{n+1} with v₁ = v₂ on Z ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}. Let y ∈ Z be a Lebesgue density point of Z (L^{n+1}(Z ∩ B̄_r(y))/L^{n+1}(B̄_r(y)) → 1) at which both are differentiable. Then Dv₁(y) = Dv₂(y).
 Proof: fix a unit vector e. By the sibling density_directions (Lean dor_lmbsf_density_directions), there are y_i ∈ Z ∖ {y} with y_i → y and (y_i − y)/|y_i − y| → e. Then 0 = ((v₁ − v₂)(y_i) − (v₁ − v₂)(y))/|y_i − y| → D(v₁ − v₂)(y)e.
 For Borel Z, a.e. point of Z is a density point (Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div_of_measurableSet), and Lipschitz functions are differentiable a.e. (Rademacher). So Dv₁ = Dv₂ a.e. on Z.
 (b) Let v₁ be the McShane extension of (f∘ψ)|_{C'}, v₂ := F (Lipschitz on C'; replace it by its McShane extension from C'), and Z := Y. By (a), for a.e. y ∈ Y ⊆ int C', f∘ψ is differentiable at y with D(f∘ψ)(y) = DF(y). The extensions agree with the originals near y ∈ int C'.
 (c) Chain rule.
 - Let y be as in (b) with F(y) ∉ {a, b}. γ is differentiable at F(y) = (f∘ψ)(y) with derivative γ'(F(y)), so Dū(y) = D(γ∘(f∘ψ))(y) = γ'(F(y))DF(y).
 - For κ ∈ {a, b}, ū ≡ γ(κ) on Z_κ := Y ∩ F⁻¹(κ), a Borel set, because f∘ψ = κ there. By (a) with v₁ = ū and v₂ ≡ γ(κ), Dū(y) = 0 = γ'(κ)DF(y) for a.e. y ∈ Z_κ.
 Hence ∇ū(y) = γ'(F(y))∇F(y) for L^{n+1}-a.e. y ∈ Y.

5. Conclusion.
 - By steps 2–4, lim_k ∫_{ψ(Y)} w Dh_k[W] dH^{n+1} = ∫_Y J(y) w(ψ(y)) γ'(F(y)) DF(y)[E(y)] dy.
 - For a.e. y ∈ Y: DF(y)[E(y)] = ⟨G(ψ(y)), A(y)E(y)⟩ = ⟨G(ψ(y)), W(ψ(y))⟩ and F(y) = f(ψ(y)).
 - Apply the Bochner area formula of step 2 backwards to the integrand x ↦ w(x)γ'(f(x))⟨G(x), W(x)⟩. The right side becomes
 ∫_{ψ(Y)} w(x) γ'(f(x)) ⟨G(x), W(x)⟩ dH^{n+1}(x) = ∫_{ψ(Y)∩{a<f<b}} w(x)·(−(b − a)⁻¹⟨G(x), W(x)⟩) dH^{n+1}(x).
 (Integrability is not needed for this identity of Bochner integrals. It holds anyway: G∘ψ = AΓ⁻¹∇F is bounded on the compact C and w is integrable.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Compact neighbourhood C' ⊆ V of C: ψ is Lipschitz and Dψ, Γ⁻¹ are bounded there. u_k = h_k∘ψ → u = (γ∘f)∘ψ uniformly.
Area formula: the integral over ψ(Y) equals ∫⟨Ŵ, ∇u_k⟩ with Ŵ = 1_Y·(w∘ψ)·J·Γ⁻¹DψᵀW ∈ L¹. Null sets transfer because J > 0.
Integration by parts for Lipschitz functions plus L¹-density of test fields: ∇u_k → ∇ū weakly-*.
Density-point agreement lemma via density_directions: D(f∘ψ) = DF a.e. on Y, and the derivative vanishes a.e. on level sets.
Chain rule: ∇ū = γ'(F)∇F a.e. on Y.
Read back through DF·E = ⟨G, W⟩ and the area formula to get the limit over ψ(Y) ∩ {a < f < b}.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent Steps 0, 4(b) (second and third bullets), 4(d), 5, 6, 7, 8 and 10; Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 4.1, Remark 4.2, 4.3, Definition 4.4 and the proof of Lemma 4.5(1). Notation: Hᵏ = μHE[k], μ_T := RT.measure = θH^{n+1}⌞M, τ(R)(ω) := R.action ω.

0. Preliminaries.
 (a) θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^{n+1} < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (locallyIntegrable_mult). For Borel W, μ_T(W) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^{n+1} (withDensity_apply).
 (b) For H^{n+1}-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) is a unit orientation of T_xM (field `orients` and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique). A unit orientation ζ of any subspace satisfies |ζ(α)| ≤ ‖α‖, so ‖ζ‖ ≤ 1.
 (c) Let ξ₀ := RT.aestronglyMeasurable_orient.mk, a strongly measurable map with ξ₀ = ξ H^{n+1}-a.e. on M.
 [Formalization note: MultiVector P k has a Borel σ-algebra, but SecondCountableTopology/FiniteDimensional instances are not synthesized automatically. So build every multivector-valued map below as a strongly measurable map, by composing strongly measurable maps with continuous maps (Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable, StronglyMeasurable.prodMk, StronglyMeasurable.piecewise / indicator on measurable sets). Real-, ℝ^P- and [0,∞]-valued strongly measurable maps are measurable (.measurable).]
 [Lean construction hints:
 - Write RT.aestronglyMeasurable_orient.mk RT.orient (mk takes the function explicitly).
 - Norms of MultiVector-valued maps may need explicit types, e.g. StronglyMeasurable.norm (β := MultiVector P (n+1)).
 - Nested continuous-linear-map types over Covector may fail instance synthesis. So build α ↦ v♭∧α as a continuous linear map with LinearMap.mkContinuous, or via ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFinCLM. Get the bound from norm_alternatizeUncurryFin_le, and get joint continuity in (v, α) and (ζ, v) from isBoundedBilinearMap_comp, isBoundedBilinearMap_smulRight and isBoundedBilinearMap_apply.]
 (d) Compact exhaustion: K_1 ⊆ K_2 ⊆ … compact with K_i ⊆ int K_{i+1} and ⋃_i K_i = U. Every compact K ⊆ U lies in some K_i.

1. Transfer of null sets to slices. Let Z be Borel with H^{n+1}(M ∩ Z) = 0. By (G3) with φ = 1_Z, ∫_ℝ Hⁿ(M_t ∩ Z) dt = ∫_M |g|1_Z dH^{n+1} = 0. As the integrand is a.e.-measurable, Hⁿ(M_t ∩ Z) = 0 for a.e. t (lintegral_eq_zero_iff').
 Let Z₀ be a Borel set with H^{n+1}(M ∩ Z₀) = 0 containing every x ∈ M at which one of the following fails: ξ(x) = ξ₀(x); ξ(x) is a unit orientation of T_xM; ‖ξ₀(x)‖ ≤ 1; g(x) ∈ T_xM. Such a set exists by (G2), 0(b), 0(c) and exists_measurable_superset_of_null applied to μHE[n+1]⌞M. Only the statement “∀ᵐ t, t ∈ G₁” below is used; G₁ need not be measurable.

2. Good levels (parent Steps 4(b), 4(d)). Let G₁ be the set of t ∈ ℝ with ∫_{M_t∩K_i} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every i and Hⁿ(M_t ∩ Z₀) = 0.
 - By (G3) with φ = θ1_{K_i} (Borel) and (G1), ∫_ℝ ∫_{M_t∩K_i} θ dHⁿ dt = ∫_{M∩K_i} |g|θ dH^{n+1} ≤ L∫_{M∩K_i} θ < ∞. So for each i, ∫_{M_t∩K_i} θ < ∞ for a.e. t.
 - With step 1 and a countable intersection, a.e. t ∈ ℝ lies in G₁.
 - For t ∈ G₁ and compact K ⊆ U, take K ⊆ K_i. Then ∫_{M_t∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞, and since θ ≥ 1, Hⁿ(M_t ∩ K) < ∞.

3. Orientation of the slices (parent Step 5; Simon 4.3).
 - For x ∈ M with g(x) ≠ 0 let ν(x) := g(x)/|g(x)| and ξ̃(x) := ξ₀(x) ∘ (α ↦ ν(x)♭∧α). This is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors, the composition of ξ₀(x) with the continuous linear map α ↦ alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ ν(x)).smulRight α).
 - Otherwise let ξ̃(x) := 0.
 - ξ̃ is strongly measurable. It is the indicator of the measurable set M ∩ {g ≠ 0} applied to x ↦ Ξ(ξ₀(x), ν(x)), where Ξ(ζ, v) := ζ ∘L (α ↦ v♭∧α) is continuous on MultiVector P (n+1) × ℝ^P, ξ₀ is strongly measurable, and ν = g/|g| is measurable into ℝ^P, hence strongly measurable.
 - Linearity of v ↦ v♭∧α gives |g(x)|·ξ̃(x)(α) = ξ₀(x)(g(x)♭∧α) for x ∈ M with g(x) ≠ 0. If g(x) = 0 then g(x)♭∧α = 0.
 Claim: for t ∈ G₁ and Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_t, M_t has approximate tangent space Q_x := T_xM ∩ g(x)^⊥ at x, and ξ̃(x) is a unit orientation of Q_x.
 - The first part is (G4b), which applies by step 2.
 - For x ∈ M_t ∖ Z₀, which is Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_t since t ∈ G₁: ξ₀(x) = ξ(x) is a unit orientation of T_xM and ν(x) ∈ T_xM is a unit vector. The sibling wedge_orientation (Lean dor_lmbsf_interior_product_orientation, with ζ := ξ₀(x), ζ' := ξ̃(x), Q := T_xM, ν := ν(x)) shows that ξ̃(x) is a unit orientation of T_xM ⊓ (ℝ∙ν(x))ᗮ = Q_x, as ℝ∙ν(x) = ℝ∙g(x).

4. The family (parent Step 6). For t ∈ G₁ let R_t := (M_t, θ, ξ̃). It is an IMRep U n:
 - M_t is Borel (M and g Borel, f continuous), M_t ⊆ M ⊆ U, and M_t is countably n-rectifiable by (G4a);
 - θ is measurable and θ > 0 on M_t ⊆ M;
 - ∫_{M_t∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (step 2);
 - ξ̃ is strongly measurable (step 3), hence a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M_t;
 - `orients` holds by step 3.
 For t ∉ G₁ let R_t be the empty triple (carrier ∅, mult 1, orient 0). It satisfies all fields vacuously: ∅ is countably n-rectifiable, and integrals and a.e. statements over ∅ are trivial. Define Rs t := R_t; membership in G₁ is decided classically.
 (1) holds: M_t ⊆ f⁻¹(t) and ∅ ⊆ f⁻¹(t).
 For t ∈ G₁ and Borel W: μ_{R_t}(W) = ∫_{M_t∩W} θ dHⁿ and τ(R_t)(ω) = ∫_{M_t} θ ξ̃(ω) dHⁿ. For t ∉ G₁ both are 0.

5. (2) (Simon 4.5(1)). Let W be Borel. By (G3) with φ = θ1_W, t ↦ ∫_{M_t∩W} θ dHⁿ is a.e.-measurable. It agrees with t ↦ μ_{R_t}(W) on the full-measure set G₁, so the latter is a.e.-measurable, and, using (G1),
 ∫_ℝ μ_{R_t}(W) dt = ∫_ℝ ∫_{M_t} θ1_W dHⁿ dt = ∫_M |g|θ1_W dH^{n+1} ≤ L∫_{M∩W} θ dH^{n+1} = Lμ_T(W).

6. (3) (parent Step 8). Fix ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), K := tsupport ω (compact ⊆ U), c := sup_x ‖ω(x)‖, and q := θ·ξ̃(ω), a Borel function (strongly measurable and real-valued).
 - Bound. For t ∈ G₁, |q| ≤ cθ1_K Hⁿ-a.e. on M_t (step 3 and 0(b)). So q is Hⁿ⌞M_t-integrable and τ(R_t)(ω) = ∫_{M_t} q⁺ dHⁿ − ∫_{M_t} q⁻ dHⁿ, both finite.
 - Measurability. By (G3) applied to the Borel functions q⁺, q⁻ ≥ 0, both terms are a.e.-measurable in t. Hence s ↦ τ(R_s)(ω) is a.e. strongly measurable; it is 0 off G₁.
 - Integrability. By step 5 with W = K, ∫_ℝ |τ(R_s)(ω)| ds ≤ c∫_ℝ μ_{R_s}(K) ds ≤ cLμ_T(K) < ∞.

7. (4') (parent Step 10; Simon 4.2). Fix ω, a < b, K, c as in step 6 and q̃ := θ·ξ̃(ω)·1_{a<f<b}, a Borel function.
 - Bound off the slices. On (M ∖ Z₀) ∩ {g ≠ 0}, |ξ̃(x)(α)| ≤ ‖ξ₀(x)‖·‖ν(x)♭∧α‖ ≤ (n+1)‖α‖, using ‖ξ₀(x)‖ ≤ 1 and ‖v♭∧α‖ ≤ (n+1)|v|‖α‖ from the alternating-sum formula. So |g||q̃| ≤ (n+1)cLθ1_K H^{n+1}-a.e. on M, which is integrable.
 - Bound on the slices. For t ∈ G₁, |q̃| ≤ cθ1_K Hⁿ-a.e. on M_t (step 6).
 - Co-area. Apply (G3) to q̃⁺ and q̃⁻ and subtract the two finite identities:
 ∫_M |g| q̃ dH^{n+1} = ∫_ℝ (∫_{M_t} q̃⁺ dHⁿ − ∫_{M_t} q̃⁻ dHⁿ) dt = ∫_ℝ ∫_{M_t} q̃ dHⁿ dt.
 - Right side. For t ∈ G₁, f ≡ t on M_t, so ∫_{M_t} q̃ dHⁿ = 1_{(a,b)}(t)·τ(R_t)(ω). Hence the right side is ∫_{(a,b)} τ(R_t)(ω) dt = ∫_a^b τ(R_s)(ω) ds: the interval integral is over (a, b] (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le), which differs from (a, b) by a null set (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo), and the integrand is integrable by (3). The real integrals are obtained from the lintegrals by integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part / integral_toReal.
 - Left side. For x ∈ M ∖ Z₀ with g(x) ≠ 0: |g(x)|ξ̃(x)(ω(x)) = ξ₀(x)(g(x)♭∧ω(x)) = ξ(x)(g(x)♭∧ω(x)). Where g(x) = 0, both |g|q̃ and θξ(g♭∧ω) vanish. Therefore ∫_M |g|q̃ dH^{n+1} = ∫_{M∩{a<f<b}} θ ξ(g♭∧ω) dH^{n+1}.
 Together these give (4'). ∎
proof_key_steps: Null sets of H^{n+1}⌞M meet a.e. slice in an Hⁿ-null set, by (G3) with φ = 1_Z.
Good levels G₁ (full measure): locally θHⁿ-finite slices avoiding the Borel bad set Z₀.

ξ̃ = ξ₀(ν♭∧·) with ν = g/|g| is strongly measurable (ξ₀ = RT.aestronglyMeasurable_orient.mk). By (G4b) and wedge_orientation it orients T_xM ∩ g^⊥, the approximate tangent space of M_t, Hⁿ-a.e. for t ∈ G₁.
R_t = (M_t, θ, ξ̃) for t ∈ G₁ and the empty triple otherwise; this gives (1).
(2) from (G3) with φ = θ1_W and |g| ≤ L.
(3): |τ(R_s)(ω)| ≤ sup‖ω‖·μ_{R_s}(tsupport ω); measurability from (G3) applied to q^±.
(4'): co-area with the signed integrand θξ̃(ω)1_{a<f<b}, f ≡ t on M_t, and |g|ξ̃(ω) = ξ(g♭∧ω).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Steps 1, 2 and 3 (definition of g and 3(a)); Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2, Remark 1.3, Remark 1.5(2) and Definition 2.1; Ch. 2, Theorems 1.2, 1.5 and §4. Notation: H^{n+1} = μHE[n+1] (= L^{n+1} on ℝ^{n+1}); for a chart ψ and y in its domain, Q(y) := Dψ(y)(ℝ^{n+1}).

1. Submanifold cover. By the sibling c1_cover (Lean dor_lmbsf_rectifiable_c1_cover, m = n+1): M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_l N_l with H^{n+1}(N₀) = 0 and each N_l satisfying IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 (n+1) N_l.

2. Countably many charts. Fix l. For each z ∈ N_l the definition gives an open V ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}, an open W ∋ z and ψ, C¹ on V, injective on V, with Dψ injective on V and ψ(V) = W ∩ N_l. N_l is Lindelöf (a subspace of the second countable ℝ^P), so countably many of these W cover N_l. Replace each V by V' := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(U), open because ψ is continuous on the open set V (ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage). Then ψ(V') ⊆ U and W ∩ N_l ∩ U ⊆ ψ(V'). Collecting over l we obtain countably many charts (V^s, ψ^s), s ∈ ℕ, satisfying (a), with M ∖ N₀ ⊆ ⋃_s ψ^s(V^s) (because M ⊆ U).

3. Balls and C¹ approximation. Fix s, write V = V^s, ψ = ψ^s. Let 𝔅_s be the countable family of closed balls B̄ = B̄_r(c) with c ∈ ℚ^{n+1}, r ∈ ℚ, r > 0 and B̄_{2r}(c) ⊆ V; it covers V. For B̄ ∈ 𝔅_s put B̄' := B̄_{2r}(c). Dψ is continuous on V, hence bounded by some Λ on the compact convex B̄', so ψ is Λ-Lipschitz on B̄' (mean value inequality) and u := f∘ψ is LΛ-Lipschitz on B̄'. Let ũ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ be a Lipschitz extension of u|_{B̄} (Ch. 2, Theorem 1.2; McShane). By the sibling c1_approx (Lean dor_lmbsf_lipschitz_c1_approx) with ε = 1/k, for every k ≥ 1 there is a C¹ function G_k with L^{n+1}({ũ ≠ G_k}) < 1/k. The set B̄ ∖ ⋃_k {u = G_k} is contained in ⋂_k {ũ ≠ G_k}, so it is L^{n+1}-null, and its image under ψ (Lipschitz on B̄) is H^{n+1}-null (SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn).

4. Indexing. Enumerate the countably many triples (s, B̄, k) as j ∈ ℕ (if there are only finitely many, pad with V_j = C_j = Y_j := ∅, ψ_j := 0, F_j := 0; all claims are then vacuous for these j). Put V_j := V^s, ψ_j := ψ^s, C_j := B̄ ∩ {u = G_k} (a closed subset of B̄, hence compact, and C_j ⊆ V_j), C'_j := B̄' (compact, C_j ⊆ B̄ ⊆ int C'_j, C'_j ⊆ V_j), F_j := G_k, E_j := ψ_j(C_j) (compact). By steps 1–3, every x ∈ M ∖ N₀ is ψ^s(v) with v in some B̄ ∈ 𝔅_s, and either v ∈ C_j for some j or v lies in the null set of step 3. Hence H^{n+1}(M ∖ ⋃_j E_j) = 0.

5. Disjoint pieces (Remark 1.3). M_j := (M ∩ E_j) ∖ ⋃_{i<j} E_i are Borel, pairwise disjoint, and ⋃_j M_j = M ∩ ⋃_j E_j. Put Y_j := C_j ∩ ψ_j⁻¹(M_j). 0. Preliminaries.
 (a) M is Borel, M ⊆ U and M is countably (n+1)-rectifiable (fields of RT).
 (b) θ(x) ≥ 1 on M (positive integer), so H^{n+1}(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^{n+1} < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (locallyIntegrable_mult).
 (c) If M has approximate tangent space Q at x, then T_xM = approxTangentPlane (n+1) M x = Q: by definition approxTangentPlane chooses some approximate tangent space, which equals Q by uniqueness (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1); SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique).

1. Pieces. Apply chart_pieces to (U, M, f, L) using (a), (b) and (TL). We obtain V_j, C_j, Y_j, ψ_j, F_j and a Borel g with properties (a)–(e) there. (G1) is part of (e). Put P_j := ψ_j(Y_j).
 - P_j is Borel (Lusin–Souslin: ψ_j is continuous and injective on the Borel set Y_j).
 - The P_j are pairwise disjoint and contained in M, and H^{n+1}(M ∖ ⋃_j P_j) = 0.
 - ψ_j(C_j) is compact and ψ_j(C_j) ⊆ ψ_j(V_j) ⊆ U.
 For each j, the data (V, C, Y, ψ, F, f, G) := (V_j, C_j, Y_j, ψ_j, F_j, f, g) satisfy all hypotheses of piece_coarea, piece_slice_tangent and piece_weak_limit: (a), (b), (d), (e) of chart_pieces; g Borel; f L-Lipschitz.

2. (G2) holds everywhere. For x = ψ_j(y) ∈ P_j: M has approximate tangent space range Dψ_j(y) at x (chart_pieces (d)), so T_xM = range Dψ_j(y) by 0(c), and g(x) ∈ range Dψ_j(y) by (e). For x ∉ ⋃_j P_j, g(x) = 0 ∈ T_xM.

3. Slices decompose. g = 0 off ⋃_j P_j and P_j ⊆ M, so M_t = ⋃_j S^j_t (disjoint), where S^j_t := P_j ∩ {g ≠ 0} ∩ f⁻¹(t) is the set S_t of the piece siblings for piece j. Each S^j_t is Borel: P_j is Borel (step 1), {g ≠ 0} is Borel since g is Borel, and f⁻¹(t) is closed since f is continuous. Likewise M_t is Borel.

4. (G3). Let φ ≥ 0 be Borel.
 - For every t, ∫_{M_t} φ dHⁿ = Σ_j ∫_{S^j_t} φ dHⁿ (lintegral over a countable disjoint union of measurable sets).
 - By piece_coarea each t ↦ ∫_{S^j_t} φ dHⁿ is a.e.-measurable; hence so is the sum.
 - By monotone convergence (lintegral_tsum) and piece_coarea:
 ∫_ℝ ∫_{M_t} φ dHⁿ dt = Σ_j ∫_ℝ ∫_{S^j_t} φ dHⁿ dt = Σ_j ∫_{P_j} |g|φ dH^{n+1} = ∫_M |g|φ dH^{n+1},
 the last equality because M is the disjoint union of the P_j and an H^{n+1}-null set.

5. (G4a). By piece_slice_tangent (i), each S^j_t is countably n-rectifiable. M_t = ⋃_j S^j_t is countably n-rectifiable, as a countable union of countably n-rectifiable sets (SimonGMT Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_iUnion).

6. (G4b). Let t be such that Hⁿ(M_t ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Fix j.
 - S^j_t ⊆ M_t ∩ ψ_j(C_j) with ψ_j(C_j) compact ⊆ U, so Hⁿ(S^j_t) < ∞.
 - By piece_slice_tangent (ii), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S^j_t, with x = ψ_j(y), S^j_t has approximate tangent space range Dψ_j(y) ∩ g(x)^⊥. By step 2 this is T_xM ∩ g(x)^⊥.
 - Apply (TL) with (U, A, B) := (U, S^j_t, M_t): both Borel, S^j_t ⊆ M_t ⊆ U, and M_t is locally Hⁿ-finite in U. So for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S^j_t, M_t has the same approximate tangent space T_xM ∩ g(x)^⊥.
 Since M_t = ⋃_j S^j_t and a countable union of null sets is null, (G4b) follows.

7. (G5). Fix a < b, (h_k), c, W, K, c' as in (G5), and let w := θ (as a real function; Borel).
 - Integrability on pieces. ∫_{P_j} θ ≤ ∫_{M∩ψ_j(C_j)} θ < ∞, so w is integrable on P_j.
 - Tangency on pieces. For H^{n+1}-a.e. x = ψ_j(y) ∈ P_j, W(x) ∈ T_xM = range Dψ_j(y), by step 2.
 - piece_weak_limit therefore gives, for every j,
 I_j(k) := ∫_{P_j} θ Dh_k[W] dH^{n+1} → I_j := ∫_{P_j∩{a<f<b}} θ·(−(b − a)⁻¹⟨g, W⟩) dH^{n+1}.
 - Domination. |θ Dh_k[W]| ≤ c c' θ 1_K, which is integrable on M by 0(b). Hence |I_j(k)| ≤ β_j := c c'·(∫⁻_{P_j∩K} θ dH^{n+1}).toReal, and Σ_j β_j ≤ c c'·(∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dH^{n+1}).toReal < ∞ (the P_j are disjoint subsets of M).
 - Summation. M is the disjoint union of the P_j and a null set, so ∫_M θ Dh_k[W] = Σ_j I_j(k) (MeasureTheory.integral_iUnion for an integrable function). Likewise ∫_{M∩{a<f<b}} θ(−(b − a)⁻¹⟨g, W⟩) = Σ_j I_j, the integrand being bounded by L c'(b − a)⁻¹ θ 1_K.
 - Dominated convergence for series (tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence) gives Σ_j I_j(k) → Σ_j I_j, which is (G5). ∎
